title: Company outcome-to-deliverable mapper and cross-functional commitment tracker
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Leadership and execs frequently ask for a single, defensible mapping from company-level outcomes to the measurable deliverables that engineering and product teams actually ship. Current artifacts are fragmented across decks, Confluence pages, and team OKR spreadsheets, and there is no lightweight protocol for teams to surface temporary capacity trades (e.g., shift 2 engineers for two sprints to unblock a high-impact initiative).

Goal: Build a pragmatic outcome-to-deliverable mapper and commitment tracker that:
- Generates a compact, auditable table mapping each company-level objective and key result to 1) prioritized deliverables, 2) owning teams, 3) committed delivery windows, and 4) capacity-trade signals.
- Supports quick cross-functional negotiation for capacity trades with audit trail and rollback (canary-style trade windows).
- Provides a dashboard view (heatband map) for execs to see concentration of risk and overloaded teams by quarter.

Solution overview: We will prototype a two-part workflow: 1) a lightweight mapping workbook (CSV/Confluence template) with enforced fields and validation rules; 2) a companion tracker service (internal-only UI + webhook-driven API) that teams use to post commitments and trade requests. The tracker will emit events consumed by the roadmap dashboard and the weekly alignment digest.

Acceptance criteria:
- Template is adopted by 6 pilot teams and yields a consolidated mapping for all company-level OKRs for the quarter.
- Tracker supports create/update/delete of commitment records, records who approved a trade, and exposes change history.
- Dashboard shows heatband map with filters by objective, team, and week; refresh latency < 5 minutes.
- Playbook for capacity-trade negotiation and rollback is documented and approved by GTM and Eng managers.

Non-goals: This ticket does not replace detailed sprint planning tooling or the full OKR cadence; it focuses on mid-level mapping (company -> deliverable -> team commitment) and rapid trades.

Artifacts and links:
- Confluence spec (draft): https://confluence.company/research/pm/outcome-mapper-draft
- Prototype workbook (Drive): https://drive.company/drive/folders/1OutcomeMapperPrototype
- Roadmap dashboard mock: https://figma.com/file/roadmap-heatband-mock
- Implementation PR (server): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1423

Key decisions to date:
- Use a spreadsheet-first approach to lower friction for teams; adoption > UI-first.
- Track approvals at the manager level (team leads + PM) for capacity trades; escalate to director if >2 sprints.
- Represent trade requests as timeboxed commitments rather than permanent reassignments.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Teams treat trades as permanent headcount changes. Mitigation: Require expiry date and auto-revert reminders; include template language in the commit record.
- Risk: Execs misinterpret heatband intensity as a directive. Mitigation: Add a clear legend and decision notes; include confidence scores for each mapping.

Next steps:
1) Finalize Confluence template and validation rules (owner: Marco).
2) Spin up tracker PoC (backend API + lightweight front-end) and seed with pilot teams.
3) Run two-week pilot with Growth, Inference Runtime, and Console teams.
4) Iterate on dashboard and playbook, plan Q2 roll-out.

Estimated stakeholders to notify on roll-out: CTO, VP Product, Eng Managers, Solutions Engineering.
